skill.name: animation-vocabulary
skill.description: Maps vague descriptions of web motion effects to precise animation terminology and explains differences between close glossary terms.
skill.summary: Identify the precise name for a described web animation or motion effect.
skill.author: emilkowalski

content.value_statement: Vague motion descriptions make design discussions and AI prompts unclear. This skill maps observed web animation behavior to precise terms and distinguishes close alternatives.
actual_capabilities: Maps vague visual or physical descriptions to glossary terms.
Returns the best matching term with a concise definition.
Ranks up to two close alternatives when a description is ambiguous.
Contrasts related concepts such as morph, crossfade, and shared element transition.
Combines glossary terms to describe effects without an exact single match.
limitations: Names effects but does not design, code, or test animations.
Uses only the included glossary and does not invent terminology.
Accuracy depends on the detail and clarity of the user's description.
The curated glossary may omit newer or specialized animation terms.

use_cases.title: Label Prototype Motion
use_cases.description: Identify the correct term for motion observed in a product prototype or reference interface.

use_cases.title: Clarify Implementation Requests
use_cases.description: Translate stakeholder descriptions into established motion terms before discussing implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve AI Prompts
use_cases.description: Replace vague animation language with precise terminology in prompts for design and development assistants.

prompt_templates.title: Name a Simple Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: What is the animation term for this effect: [describe what moves, when it starts, and how it feels]?
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you need one likely term for a clear effect.

prompt_templates.title: Find Close Matches
prompt_templates.prompt: Name the best glossary term for [effect description]. Include up to two alternatives and explain how they differ.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several motion patterns may fit the description.

prompt_templates.title: Disambiguate Two Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [term one] and [term two] for this interaction: [description]. State which term fits best and why.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you already know two possible terms.

prompt_templates.title: Decompose Complex Motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this interaction into glossary terms: [detailed sequence]. Order the terms by event and mark any approximate match.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for multi-stage motion with entrances, transitions, feedback, or physics.

output_examples.input: A menu grows from the button that opened it instead of expanding from its center.
output_examples.output: Origin-aware animation - The element animates from its trigger rather than its default center.

output_examples.input: One image seems to turn into another image.
output: Best match: Morph - One shape smoothly turns into another.
Alternative: Crossfade - The images only fade over each other.
Alternative: Shared element transition - The image also travels or changes position.

output_examples.input: Cards enter one after another with a short delay.
output_examples.output: Stagger - Several items animate sequentially with a small delay, creating a cascade.

best_practices: Describe what moves, its direction, its timing, and how the motion feels.
Provide the interaction context, such as opening, scrolling, dragging, or navigation.
Ask for alternatives when the observed effect could match several glossary terms.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to generate production animation code.
Do not expect a precise match from a description that omits visible behavior.
Do not treat related terms as interchangeable without checking their differences.

faq.question: Does this skill create animations?
faq.answer: No. It identifies and explains animation terms but does not design or implement effects.

faq.question: Can it identify an effect from an informal description?
faq.answer: Yes. Describe what you see or feel, and it will select the closest glossary term.

faq.question: What happens when several terms fit?
faq.answer: It lists the best match first and may provide up to two alternatives with brief distinctions.

faq.question: Will it invent a missing animation term?
faq.answer: No. It states when the glossary lacks an exact match and uses known terms for an approximation.

faq.question: Can it compare similar animation concepts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain differences between close terms such as clip-path and mask.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is listed as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
